A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CIM research and contain readable main text, references, and supplementary Sections 6–8. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of all equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original captioning experiments, metric-validation results, ablations, robustness analyses, and qualitative examples in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 2–7 and qualitative examples in Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The retrieval procedure, GRC and QIR components, combined reward, and GRPO optimization in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain RefinedCaps and DOCCI training, DenseFusion retrieval corpora, COCO-LN500 and DOCCI500 evaluation, and Oxford-IIIT Pet verification. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–7, including base models, SFT, SC-Captioner, ShareCaptioner, Gemini-1.5, Claude-3.7, and larger-model comparisons.

E3.justification: Training budgets, sample counts, model configurations, retrieval settings, evaluation metrics, and prompts remain identical in Section 4.1 and supplementary Sections 6–7.

E4.justification: The reward-component ablation, retrieval-corpus scaling study, encoder robustness comparisons, and supplementary qualitative examples are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same Pearson correlations and 100-sample binning. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the supplement. For example, Table 2 reports the same Qwen2.5-VL-7B+CIM COCO-LN500 scores of 48.93 CAPTURE and 44.15 Relations QA in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged, including GRC, QIR, the combined reward, and normalized advantage in Equations 1–4. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about annotation-free caption-quality rewards, CIM, and improved captioning performance. The abstract's code-release update concerns availability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of precision–recall tradeoffs, stronger models' reinforcement-learning gains, corpus scaling, and encoder robustness remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code upon acceptance with a statement that code is released and a GitHub repository hyperlink. This adds concrete access information; implementation settings and supplementary prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 generalizes its description of CapRL [74]'s reward from downstream VQA accuracy to downstream task performance. This is a limited related-work framing revision; the bibliography and overall novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds Kaifu Zhang's affiliation marker, updates the code-availability sentence, and makes localized wording and punctuation edits in Section 2.2. The section structure and remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their content and placement. Section 2.2 has minor text reflow, including a new unresolved '?' citation marker and a closing bracket wrapped onto a separate line.

improvement.justification: The concrete GitHub link replacing an acceptance-contingent release promise modestly improves reproducibility guidance. Scientific content and appendix evidence remain unchanged. The new unresolved citation slightly reduces presentation quality, but the access information provides a limited net benefit. Repository contents cannot be assessed from the supplied PDFs.
